Subject: Chat degradation: p99 spikes during morning peak

Marcus —

We're seeing a large spike in tail latency on the streaming chat endpoint during our morning peak window (08:45–09:30 ET). p50 is fine (~120ms), p95 is elevated (~780ms), but p99 has jumped to ~3.2s for a sustained 20-minute window. This is impacting our triage agents — messages are delayed and some conversations time out.

Quick notes: 
- Occurred across multiple regions (US-east primarily).
- Only occurs on the SSE endpoint; websocket usage is also affected for some customers.
- Happened after a high-volume campaign; concurrent connections were up ~2.5x.

Attached is a short log snippet we captured from our client showing spikes and a couple of server-side 503s. Can you confirm whether this is on Redwood's side or something we should mitigate client-side?

We need: an ETA for mitigation + whether we should switch to polling temporarily.

Thanks,
Helen
Head of Ops, Brightline Health

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Chat degradation: p99 spikes during morning peak

Quick triage (observations):
- Confirmed: p99 tail correlates with high concurrent SSE connections (>18k for Brightline in us-east) plus a notable shift to longer context lengths (median token count ~840; 12% > 1,200 tokens).
- Root-candidate: KV-cache churn / eviction under heavy open-KV sets, which amplifies per-request kernel launches for longer sequences. We also see request packing latency jumps when burst arrival rate exceeds our packing window assumptions.
- Errors: a small number of 503s consistent with transient scheduling/backpressure at the serving layer.

Mitigation plan (IMMEDIATE, non-breaking):
1) Short-term routing: route 25% of Brightline streaming sessions to a lower-memory quantized variant (redwood-compact-v1-q4) to reduce per-connection footprint.
2) Reduce continuous-batching window from 12ms -> 6ms for affected hosts to bound tail amplification.
3) Pin most-frequent KV keys for Brightline traffic to reduce eviction churn.

I can push (1)+(2) as a targeted config change now; (3) requires 20–40 minutes to compute a safe pin list and deploy. Expect visible p99 improvement in ~5–15 minutes post-change for routing + batch window.

Attachments: heatmap and p99 timeseries from console.

— Lauren
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Rishi / Hannah — quick executive summary and asks.

What happened: Brightline observed sustained p99 spikes (~3s) on streaming chat during morning peak. Root candidates: KV-cache churn + packing-window amplification under 2.5x normal concurrency. Some 503s surfaced.

Immediate mitigations we want to enact (lauren can perform on approval):
- Route 25% of Brightline sessions to redwood-compact-v1-q4 (non-breaking; model parity acceptable for their use case).
- Reduce batching window for affected hosts (12ms -> 6ms).
- Schedule targeted KV-pin job (20–40 min) to reduce eviction.

Requesting: approval to (A) execute the 25% fallback routing and batch-window change (safe rollback available), and (B) approve up to 2 hours of increased Dedicated burst capacity if we see continued elevated concurrency (billing impact to be handled as a customer credit for this incident).

Customer impact: multiple agent-facing delays; potential missed conversions. Customer is asking for ETA and whether polling fallback is recommended — we will advise against polling if we can enact routing.

Decision needed: please reply with APPROVE / DECLINE for (A) + (B). I'll communicate back to Brightline immediately after you respond.

— Marcus
